questions.prompt: He urges shifting the old disease model from single nutrients in isolation toward:
choices: A Ignoring food entirely.
B Foods and dietary patterns—we eat foods, not isolated nutrients.
C Only demonizing one nutrient forever.
D Supplements replacing all meals.
questions.explain: Move from single-nutrient demonization to foods and patterns.

questions.prompt: The Standard American Diet is typically high in:
choices: A Only wild fish and olives.
B Added sugars, unhealthy fats, and refined grains (and often ultra-processed foods).
C Exclusive whole-food protein.
D Nothing linked to disease.
questions.explain: SAD: added sugars, unhealthy fats, refined grains.

questions.prompt: A practical check he likes for real food is:
choices: A Only influencer endorsements.
B Could you recreate it in your own kitchen?—real foods are the ingredients.
C Preferring the longest ingredient list.
D Avoiding all home cooking.
questions.explain: Recreatability in your kitchen marks minimally processed food.

questions.prompt: Industrial seed oils are concerning partly because:
choices: A Consumption has not changed in a century.
B Intake of some has risen enormously (e.g., about a thousandfold) versus historical baselines.
C They are identical to butter nutritionally always.
D They never appear in ultra-processed foods.
questions.explain: Some oil intakes are up on the order of 1000× versus ~100 years ago.

choices: A Isolated nutrients always outperform whole foods.
B Isolated nutrients can underperform relative to the food matrix's full compound context.
C Foods have no synergistic compounds.
D Only pills matter.
questions.explain: Isolated compounds can paradoxically underperform versus whole-food context.
